$Comment: Extends the jar's own Sawmill.json (RPG Stations), which stays live untouched; this ExtensionAsset adds to it additively via Target.Station. What this extension carries: (1) PerCycleContributions -> the sawmill's entire progression path (see below); (2) Loot.Lootables -> this pack's own SawmillLuckTiers lootable, the MMO-luck tier ladder (see that file's own $Comment for the loot-side rationale); (3) Loot.Rolls[0] -> the MMO-luck-scaled bonus-copy roll below. Nothing else: no Puppet, no Custody. PerCycleContributions: the jar's own Sawmill.json declares no contributions at all (RPG Stations is completely progression-agnostic by design - its shipped content declares no contributions of its own and ships inert, the same pattern as the vanilla Affinity_* assets), so this extension OWNS the sawmill's progression outright rather than adding a slice on top of an existing jar award. Both entries post to the mmoskilltree:skill_xp channel (Param = skill id), forwarded verbatim on the cycle-completed event and consumed by the MMO bridge, which multiplies each by the station's tool multiplier and awards it as skill XP: WOODCUTTING at 8.0/cycle, CRAFTING at 4.0/cycle. To re-tune the sawmill's XP, edit the Amounts here; RPG Stations itself never resolves or interprets the Channel string, it only forwards {Channel, Param, Amount} on Work.PerCycleContributions. Bonus-copy roll: the jar's own SawmillFinds.json carries a tool_power-scaled bonus-copy roll, and this roll adds a second one scaled off MMO luck instead, on the reasoning that the two scale on different axes and both should fire: the jar's stays untouched and scales off held-tool power, this one scales off MMO luck, so a better hatchet and a luckier woodcutter each earn their own independent extra plank. The roll is BasePercent 0 with a single unweighted mmoskilltree:station_luck AddFactor and no CapPercent, so effective chance is exactly the player's aggregate station luck in percent, and max luck reaches a guaranteed proc (RollEvaluator's absent-CapPercent default of 100 is the natural single-roll ceiling). The explicit "Trigger": "Cycle" matches Roll#effectiveTrigger's own reader default (behavior is identical either way) but stating it matches the jar's SawmillFinds convention and documents that BonusOutputCopies is only meaningful on a Cycle trigger. Extension Rolls are additive onto the base station's Loot (ExtensionCatalog#mergeLoot unions Lootables and Rolls); SawmillLuckTiers.json proves the mechanism from the Lootables side, this roll exercises the inline-Rolls side of the same LootRef.
